stories.t: PLA mass far-seas deployment around Taiwan, with no exercise name
stories.x: Indo-Pacific Beijing Taiwan's NSC chief Joseph Wu reported more than 100 PLA Navy and China Coast Guard vessels in the Western Pacific on 3 Nov. On 2 Nov there were 49 air sorties, the highest single day this year. AEI/ISW analysts count four task groups from the Eastern, Northern and Southern Theatre Commands between Taiwan and Guam. These include the Liaoning group, and the Fujian left Sanya on 2 Nov. Daily counts have dropped back since (4 aircraft, 6 vessels in the 24 hours to 6am on 8 Nov). This drill practises keeping outside navies out of the area, which is the job the US alliance and AUKUS force posture would face in a crisis. It also comes ahead of APEC in Shenzhen (18–19 Nov), where Albanese may go on to Beijing (SCMP, unconfirmed). A visit would test how Canberra keeps stabilisation with China going while this is underway.

stories.t: Hormuz still closed as mines hit tankers and Qatar mediates
stories.x: Middle East Tehran and Beijing Iran says two tankers caught fire after hitting mines on an "unauthorised route." Explosions were heard on Qeshm Island and at Jask, days after US strikes. CENTCOM disabled a St Kitts-flagged ship in the Gulf of Oman. Trump called Friday's strikes on Iranian air defences "minor" and is weighing a larger wave now that the midterms are over. The IRGC lifted its self-imposed 2,000 km ballistic missile range cap. Iran is reviewing Qatari proposals on its nuclear program. Australia imports most of its liquid fuel, so a long closure hits the economy directly. The RBA's 25-point hike to 4.85% cited war-driven energy costs. The ADF has given defensive support to Gulf states since March, so any escalation after the midterms raises the question of how far that commitment goes.

stories.t: Abu Dhabi talks set for 10–11 Nov after Trump meets Putin's envoy
stories.x: Europe Moscow Trump met Kirill Dmitriev at the White House and said a deal may be close, but gave no details and didn't meet the Ukrainian delegation. Witkoff says working-level talks between Russia, the US and Ukraine will cover post-war security arrangements, de-escalation and humanitarian issues. A Kremlin aide says sanctions relief for Russia's sovereign wealth fund is being discussed. The EU's Kallas rejects any deal made without Europe. Australia has sanctions on Russia and has sent Bushmasters to Ukraine. A deal that rewards taking territory by force and lifts sanctions sets a precedent that would be read closely in the Indo-Pacific. Australia would also have to decide whether to keep its own sanctions if Washington drops its.

stories.t: North Korea's fourth weapons launch in a month
stories.x: Korean Peninsula Pyongyang and Beijing KCNA reported cluster-bomb warhead tests (1 Nov), a strategic cruise missile with a dispersal warhead (2 Nov), and a new air-defence missile plus a cruise missile strike drill (4 Nov). NK News says the drill photos were heavily doctored. Talks with Washington remain in doubt. The ADF regularly sends aircraft and ships to monitor UN sanctions on North Korea. Australia is also strengthening ties with Japan and South Korea. Cluster and dispersal warheads point to battlefield use against airfields, which also matters for how Australia thinks about protecting its own bases.

stories.t: The Pacific contest: Solomons treaty, PNG explosive, Quad in Atlanta
stories.x: Pacific & near region Beijing - Canberra and Honiara have an in-principle treaty, reportedly with A$980m in extra funding. Solomon Islands keeps its security pact with China, and PM Wale faces a no-confidence motion. The ABC says a Chinese military-grade explosive found in a container in PNG is a real weapon. Chinese officials had called it a wine bottle. Quad foreign ministers (31 Oct, Atlanta) raised concerns about economic coercion and export restrictions, and announced critical minerals work and port cooperation in Fiji. A leaders' summit is planned for Manila this month. The ADF sent a C-130, a Citation and 20 personnel to help fight the East Kalimantan fires. Pacific security partnerships are where Australia competes most directly with China for influence, and where Canberra has the most to lose if partners hedge.

stories.t: Bottom line up front
stories.x: The PLA has two carriers and 100+ naval and coast guard vessels at sea east of Taiwan in an unnamed, unannounced three-theatre operation. Beijing not naming it is the signal to watch. The Strait of Hormuz is still shut. Mines hit tankers overnight and the IRGC dropped its 2,000 km missile range cap. The RBA has already blamed war-driven energy costs for its rise to 4.85%. Russia–US–Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi on 10–11 Nov. Moscow is framing them as US–Russia normalisation, and Europe says it's been sidelined.

stories.t: US extends Iran blockade to land routes as Hormuz stays shut
stories.x: MIDDLE EAST Tehran and Moscow - 7 Nov: CENTCOM announced Task Force Iron Gate, a roughly 20-person, Tampa-based cell that extends the naval blockade to Iran's land borders and the Caspian Sea. CENTCOM hasn't said whether it will run direct military operations. CENTCOM says the blockade has redirected 144 vessels and kept more than US$25b of Iranian crude off the market. 7 Nov: US forces disabled the St Kitts-flagged cargo ship M/V Huda, which CENTCOM says tried to breach the blockade. Iranian media reported two missiles hit Qeshm Island after what Trump called "minor strikes". 8 Nov: Trump told CNN that resuming all-out attacks was "highly unlikely" if Iran signs a strong deal and reopens Hormuz. He also said the US has "38 bridges" targeted and three carriers in the region. Rubio said the sides are not "on the verge of a breakthrough". Shipping: Iran says two more tankers hit mines on 7

stories.t: Russia hits Ukraine's power grid on the eve of Abu Dhabi talks
stories.x: EUROPE Moscow - Overnight 7–8 Nov: DTEK says more than 600,000 residents in Dnipropetrovsk lost power. Nearly 250,000 customers lost power in Kharkiv region. In Zhytomyr, 140 apartment blocks lost heating. Temperatures are near freezing. Ukraine's air force says it downed 137 of 164 drones launched from the evening of 7 Nov. Zelensky raised the death toll from the 2 Nov strike on an aid centre at Komyshuvakha (Zaporizhzhia) to 55, saying "more people may still be under the rubble". US envoy Witkoff says working-level talks between the US, Russia and Ukraine will run in Abu Dhabi on 10–11 Nov, covering an end to the war, post-war security arrangements and de-escalation. Witkoff and Kushner lead for the US. Zelensky accuses Moscow of escalating before the talks. Australia sanctions Russia and has supplied Bushmasters to Ukraine. A deal that rewards taking territory by force, or trades sanc

stories.t: Democrats take Congress: what it means for the alliance and AUKUS
stories.x: UNITED STATES Beijing and Moscow - Democrats won control of both the House and Senate at the 3 Nov midterms. AP tallies cited by Yahoo/CBS had them at about 54 Senate seats and 254 House seats, with races still being counted. Alaska and Mississippi Senate races are too close to call, so totals are provisional. Hakeem Jeffries is in line to become Speaker. Schumer has promised "legislative razor wire" against Trump. Reports say the House could move to impeach Defense Secretary Hegseth (unconfirmed timing). Albanese called the result "very significant", saying the Iran war and tariffs were "major factors". He said: "I will work constructively with President Trump." Congress controls US submarine-building money and has to approve transfers under AUKUS. Support for AUKUS has been bipartisan (Rep. Joe Courtney co-chairs the Friends of Australia Caucus). But a Democratic Congress focused on ov

stories.t: Japan's security rewrite draws Beijing's fire as Wong and Motegi talk Pacific
stories.x: INDO-PACIFIC Beijing - Tokyo aims to finish revising its three core security documents (National Security Strategy, National Defense Strategy, Defense Buildup Program) by year's end. Reports from October say a 3.5% of GDP spending target will be left out because it would require tax rises, but spending will still grow. Issues under review include the three non-nuclear principles and nuclear-powered submarines. 3 Nov: Penny Wong and FM Motegi met for 15 minutes at the G20 foreign ministers' meeting in Atlanta. They reaffirmed security and economic-security cooperation with a focus on the Pacific Islands, marking 50 years of the 1976 Basic Treaty. PLA activity around Taiwan has eased after last week's mass deployment: Taiwan's MND counted 4 aircraft, 6 PLAN ships and 2 official ships to 6am on 8 Nov, compared with 32 aircraft on 1 Nov. Japan is Australia's closest security partner after th

stories.t: PNG: Chinese 'artillery shell' or 'wine bottle'?
stories.x: PACIFIC Beijing - 30 Oct: PNG police and the PNG Defence Force recovered a suspected projectile from a container of building materials at a Port Moresby construction site. Taiwan's CNA reports a 32 kg, 130 mm Chinese Type 59 round and four Chinese nationals arrested (arrests not independently confirmed). 31 Oct: Police dismissed suggestions it was a dummy. 3 Nov: The Chinese embassy said it was a "shell-shaped wine bottle" that "poses no danger". The ABC, citing unnamed sources, says it is a real shell with explosive and a fuse. The US military has engaged with PNG bomb-disposal teams. PNG police have not yet released official findings. PNG is Australia's closest neighbour and a treaty partner under the 2025 Pukpuk mutual defence treaty. Any sign of Chinese military materiel moving through PNG supply chains touches Australia's core security interest. The US role in the probe also shows W

stories.t: Bottom line up front
stories.x: Washington has extended its Iran blockade to land routes and the Caspian (Task Force Iron Gate). Trump says a return to full-scale war is "highly unlikely" if Tehran deals. Hormuz is still effectively shut and Brent is near US$98. Russia blacked out more than 850,000 Ukrainian customers on the eve of the Abu Dhabi talks (10–11 Nov). Moscow says Europe has no seat at the table. Democrats now control both houses of Congress. Albanese says nothing changes in how he deals with Trump, but AUKUS funding and Iran war powers now face a hostile Congress.

stories.t: Iran: Trump meets Qatar's mediator as Tehran says the next move is Washington's
stories.x: MIDDLE EAST Tehran, Beijing and Moscow - 9 Nov (US time): Trump meets Qatari PM Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani at the White House at noon Eastern (about 4am Tuesday AEDT). Vance is also due to meet him separately. Qatar denies reports that the US–Iran talks have failed. Araghchi says Qatar-mediated talks produced a "two-day plan": the US takes agreed steps on day one and Iran reopens Hormuz on day two. Qatar's mediation cut it down from an earlier seven-day plan. Tehran wants sanctions relief and fewer US troops in the region. Araghchi's line is that it is now the White House's turn to choose. Trump told CNN that new large-scale strikes are "highly unlikely" if talks progress, but he has three carriers in the region. He told CBS: "We would have had a deal except for this election." Rubio says the talks are "not productive" and Iran's demands are "simply unacceptable". Xinhua, c

stories.t: Saudi–Houthi war escalates: village strike near Sanaa, missiles at Riyadh
stories.x: MIDDLE EAST Tehran and Moscow - 7 Nov: Airstrikes hit al-Shariya village in Bani Hushaysh, a Houthi stronghold east of Sanaa. Houthi-run Saba says at least 33 people were killed and 39 wounded, mostly women and children. Reuters could not verify the figures. Saudi Arabia's Center for International Communication says it is investigating the reports. 8 Nov: The Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted a Houthi ballistic missile aimed at the Eastern Province and two missiles fired at Riyadh. Falling debris damaged an administrative building in Riyadh's Aramco Tower. The Energy Ministry reported limited damage and no casualties. The Houthis also claim attacks on Saudi airports and Aramco storage sites. The fighting resumed in July and ended the 2022 UN-brokered truce. The IOM says more than 200,000 people have been displaced since then. With Hormuz effectively shut, Saudi exports that bypass

stories.t: Russia pounds Ukraine's grid, reportedly with North Korean missiles, before Abu Dhabi talks
stories.x: EUROPE Moscow - 7–8 Nov: Russian strikes cut power to more than 600,000 people in Dnipropetrovsk region (DTEK) and about 250,000 in Kharkiv region. The Energy Ministry says the 7 Nov attack hit five regions and disrupted transmission to Kyiv. 9 Nov: Zelensky says preliminary findings show Russia used North Korean KN-23 ballistic missiles on a key energy facility. This is the first time he has named the model in this campaign. He asked allies for more interceptors and tougher sanctions. Russia's MoD says it will keep striking fuel and energy facilities it says support Ukraine's military. It claims 430 Ukrainian drones were downed overnight. DPR head Pushilin claims advances along the Donetsk front near Druzhkovka (unverified). US-brokered US–Russia–Ukraine talks are due in Abu Dhabi on 10–11 Nov, with Witkoff and Kushner leading for the US. Deputy FM Pankin told TASS that a US–Russia "die

stories.t: China's DF-61 ICBM moves fast into routine training
stories.x: INDO-PACIFIC Beijing - 5 Nov: CCTV reported that the DF-61 road-mobile ICBM, first shown at the September 2025 parade, is in routine PLA Rocket Force training. The training covers field mobility, moving between launch positions and launch procedures. The report marked 66 years since the DF-1 launch. State media also showed the rarely seen DF-100 cruise missile. CCTV gave no range, numbers or basing. Training does not prove full operational readiness. Social media claims of an inland ICBM test, possibly including a mid-course interception, are unconfirmed (SCMP). SCMP analysts also ask whether recent PLA Navy deployments in the western Pacific and South China Sea rehearse keeping US forces out of a Taiwan conflict. Background: In September 2024 China fired a DF-31B ICBM into the South Pacific. Reports say it fired a submarine-launched missile into the Pacific in July 2026. The US and alli

stories.t: North Korea tests new missiles and wins new embassies as its missiles appear in Ukraine
stories.x: KOREAN PENINSULA Pyongyang - 5 Nov: KCNA said the Missile Administration test-fired a new surface-to-air missile system, overseen by Gen. Kim Jong Sik. Separately, a strategic cruise missile unit hit a simulated airport target. This followed a reported cluster-type cruise missile warhead test on 2 Nov. The performance claims are not independently confirmed. Belarus has opened an embassy in Pyongyang, and Brazil's first ambassador in a decade has taken up his post (NK News). North Korean loudspeakers are visible at the border again, but no broadcasts have been heard. 9 Nov: Zelensky says Russia used KN-23s on Ukraine's grid (see Europe story). Australia's latest move is not new: on 22 Oct it sanctioned Yu Pu Ung, Sim Hyon Sop and two IT firms over fake remote-work schemes that fund weapons programs. The US has since blacklisted a Seychelles-based crypto exchange over North Korean money la

stories.t: Bottom line up front
stories.x: Iran talks reach a decision point. Trump meets Qatar's PM at the White House (about 4am Tuesday AEDT). Araghchi says it is Washington's turn to choose between his "two-day" Hormuz plan and war. Rubio calls Iran's demands "simply unacceptable". The Saudi–Houthi war is the second Gulf front to watch. The Houthis say a Saudi strike killed 33 in a village near Sanaa. Missiles aimed at Riyadh and the Eastern Province were intercepted, and debris damaged Aramco Tower. Both threaten the routes oil uses to bypass Hormuz. Russia keeps hitting Ukraine's grid before the Abu Dhabi talks (10–11 Nov). Zelensky says North Korean KN-23 missiles hit a key energy site. China says its new DF-61 ICBM is already in routine training.

stories.t: Qatar takes Iran's two-day Hormuz plan to Trump; no breakthrough yet
stories.x: MIDDLE EAST Tehran and Beijing - 9 Nov (US time): Trump met Qatari PM Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani at the White House for just under an hour, behind closed doors. There was no public readout. Axios reported Qatar wanted Trump to give diplomacy more time. The proposal Qatar carried, as reported: Iran reopens Hormuz and stops attacks on Gulf tankers. In return the US lifts its naval and economic blockade and releases about US$8b of Iranian funds held in Qatar. Iran has cut its proposed implementation period from seven days to two, which spokesman Baqaei called a "sign of goodwill". Trump on 60 Minutes, asked about escalating: "I'm not looking to. I don't think there's any reason to." He said Task Force Iron Gate, which extends the blockade to land routes, "is in full force and effect". Rubio said the sides are not "at the verge of a breakthrough" and called Iran's demands "unac

stories.t: Russia, Ukraine and US resume peace talks in Abu Dhabi
stories.x: EUROPE Moscow - 10–11 Nov: US-mediated trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi, the first since the process stalled when the Iran war began in late February. Delegations: Witkoff and Kushner for the US. Ukraine sends Rustem Umerov with Kyrylo Budanov, Sergiy Kyslytsya and Davyd Arakhamia. Russia's reinforced team is led by Vladimir Medinsky and reportedly includes Sergei Ryabkov and Mikhail Galuzin. Agenda: post-war security arrangements, de-escalation and humanitarian issues. Kushner says a "comprehensive and lasting settlement" needs Russia and Europe to deal directly on security. An EU team led by Bjoern Seibert (von der Leyen's chief of staff) is attending, with E3 national security advisers, Italy and a NATO representative. Russia has not said whether it will meet them. Both sides kept striking energy targets on the eve of the talks. Zelensky says Russia used North Korean-made KN-23 missiles

stories.t: Iran announces offensive doctrine with 'no geographical limits'
stories.x: MIDDLE EAST Tehran - 9 Nov: Army spokesman Brig. Gen. Mohammad Akraminia said Iran's military doctrine has moved from a defensive to an offensive approach. "Effective response" without geographical limits is now operational strategy (ISNA, via ANI). IRNA ties this to new directives from Commander-in-Chief Mojtaba Khamenei. The same day, President Pezeshkian said the Supreme Leader had ordered officials to end the state of "neither war nor peace". He added: "We favor dialogue and negotiations... we will not surrender to force and bullying." Press TV ran an opinion piece listing possible targets: US bases across the Gulf, Jordan and Djibouti, plus Diego Garcia, undersea internet cables, energy terminals, Gulf desalination plants and Israeli nuclear and tech sites. No source formally links the doctrine announcement to Pezeshkian's remarks. The link is implied by timing. Naming Diego Garcia,

stories.t: Trump heads for APEC in Shenzhen and floats a Trump–Xi–Putin meeting
stories.x: INDO-PACIFIC Beijing and Moscow - Trump says he expects to meet Putin and Xi together during his trip to the APEC leaders' meeting in Shenzhen on 18–19 Nov: "one of the meetings I think will be with President Putin and President Xi". He says the agenda includes "denuclearization" and ending the Iran war. Peskov says "work is underway". Beijing has announced no trilateral. A Manila stop on 16 Nov has been reported (New York Post, citing the Philippine palace). This is not confirmed by the White House. SCMP reports US military transport aircraft landing in Shenzhen, widely read as preparation for the visit. 10 Nov: China's Commerce Ministry extended for two more months its suspension of export-control measures against 16 US entities (listed April 2025). It said this implements the consensus from the "eighth round" of US–China trade talks. The broader trade truce runs to January. This would

stories.t: Chinese consulate presses Victoria over killing of delivery rider in Melbourne
stories.x: AUSTRALIA Beijing - 6 Nov, about 8.10pm: a Chinese national working as a HungryPanda food-delivery rider was killed near Queen Victoria Market, Melbourne. Another rider was injured. Police say two riders confronted a man suspected of tampering with their bikes, and an altercation followed. A 51-year-old man was arrested. The Chinese Consulate-General activated its "emergency consular protection mechanism". Consul-General Fang Xinwen phoned the Victorian Premier and asked that the perpetrator be "severely punished". Global Times reports the Premier promised justice. A Weibo hashtag about the victim's long working hours drew more than 4.9 million views. SCMP reports online outrage in China over delivery-rider safety. The case is now a bilateral consular issue as well as a criminal one. Beijing's public pressure on a state premier tests how Canberra and Victoria handle Chinese official advo

stories.t: Bottom line up front
stories.x: Qatar's PM took Iran's two-day Hormuz proposal to Trump behind closed doors. No outcome has been announced. Brent fell almost 5% to about US$94 on hopes of no new strikes, but Tehran says its uranium stays in Iran and its forces now plan for a response with "no geographical limits". The first US-brokered Russia–Ukraine talks since February open in Abu Dhabi today (10–11 Nov), with EU and NATO officials nearby. Moscow says it won't accept a freeze and is casting Europe as the obstacle to peace. Trump says he expects a Trump–Xi–Putin meeting at APEC in Shenzhen (18–19 Nov), and Beijing has extended a trade-truce gesture. Closer to home, Beijing's consulate is pressing Victoria over the killing of a Chinese delivery rider in Melbourne.
